title: November Brunch Special!
subtitle: Spinach and Egg Pie with Flaky Filo Pastry
description: A perfect weekend baking project, this crunchy filo pie is one of our greatest hits! Inspired by the traditional Italian pie, torta pasqualina, it's packed with a cheesy silverbeet filling. It takes a bit more time than a regular weeknight recipe, but it's well worth the effort. Enjoy it for brunch, lunch or dinner!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 190C. Grease a 20cm round springform pan. Finely chop the onion. Finely chop the silverbeet (see Kitchen notes), keeping the leaves and stems separate. Finely chop the dill, including the stems. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Coarsely grate the cheddar. Crumble the feta.

Cook filling: Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a large deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion and silverbeet stems, stirring, for 5-6 mins until softened. Season with salt and pepper. Add the silverbeet leaves, dill and garlic and cook, stirring, for a further 1-2 mins until wilted. Transfer to a bowl and cool slightly, then stir through the cheddar and feta.

Prep pastry case: Meanwhile, melt 40g butter with 1 tbs olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Remove from the heat. Lay 1 filo sheet on the bench (see Kitchen notes). Brush with the butter mixture, then top with another filo sheet. Repeat with 5 more filo sheets. Use the filo stack to line the base and side of the pan. Using scissors, trim the filo to the rim of the pan.

Assemble pie: Spoon the filling into the pastry case. Using a spoon, make 2 egg-sized indents in the filling. Carefully crack an egg into each indent. Lay 1 filo sheet on the bench and brush with the butter mixture. Top with another filo sheet, then repeat with 1 more filo sheet. Fold in half, put on top of the filling, then trim to a circle that fits in the pan.

Bake and serve up: Fold the side of the filo pastry case down over the circle to cover. Brush the pie top with the remaining butter mixture and scatter with sesame seeds. Bake for 35-40 mins until the pastry is golden. Stand for 5 mins. Remove from the pan, transfer to a serving plate and enjoy! Serve immediately to prevent the pastry becoming soggy. Serves 3-4.

Kitchen notes: Grown for its leaves and eaten like other leafy greens, silverbeet is often called 'spinach', but is actually a close relative of beetroot. ~ To prevent the filo sticking to the bench, lay it on top of the plastic sheet from the packet. Cover the remaining filo with a damp tea towel while you work so it doesn't dry out.
